{{nihongo|'''Hinatano Shrine'''|比奈多乃神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

'''Hinatano Shrine''' (ひなたのじんじゃ, {{Lang-en|Hinatano Jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|ar|كاكيغاوا (شيزوكا)|azb|کاکهقاوا، شیزوئوکا|ce|Какегава|ceb|Kakegawa|cs|Kakegawa (Šizuoka)|de|Kakegawa|eo|Kakegaŭa|es|Kakegawa|et|Kakegawa|fa|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|fi|Kakegawa|fr|Kakegawa|gl|Kakegawa|id|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|it|Kakegawa|ja|掛川市|ko|가케가와시|mg|Kakegawa|mzn|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|nl|Kakegawa|no|Kakegawa|pl|Kakegawa|pt|Kakegawa|ro|Kakegawa|ru|Какегава|sh|Kakegava|simple|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|sr|Какегава|sv|Kakegawa|tg|Какегава|th|คาเกงาวะ|tl|Kakegawa|tr|Kakegawa|tt|Какегава|uk|Какеґава (Сідзуока)|ur|کاکیگاوا|vi|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|war|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|zh|掛川市|zh_classical|掛川市|zh_min_nan|Kakegawa-chhī|zh_yue|掛川|qid=Q823988}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}, Japan. Under the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ancient shrine ranking system}}, its rank was {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|Q134917287|qid=Q134917287}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. It was formerly also known as '''Tempaku Koma Shrine''' (てんぱくじんじゃ, {{Lang-en|Tempaku Jinja}}).

=== Overview ===
Hinatano Shrine is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Kamihijikataochiai|ja|上土方落合|qid=Q131442141}}, {{ill|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|ar|كاكيغاوا (شيزوكا)|azb|کاکهقاوا، شیزوئوکا|ce|Какегава|ceb|Kakegawa|cs|Kakegawa (Šizuoka)|de|Kakegawa|eo|Kakegaŭa|es|Kakegawa|et|Kakegawa|fa|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|fi|Kakegawa|fr|Kakegawa|gl|Kakegawa|id|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|it|Kakegawa|ja|掛川市|ko|가케가와시|mg|Kakegawa|mzn|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|nl|Kakegawa|no|Kakegawa|pl|Kakegawa|pt|Kakegawa|ro|Kakegawa|ru|Какегава|sh|Kakegava|simple|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|sr|Какегава|sv|Kakegawa|tg|Какегава|th|คาเกงาวะ|tl|Kakegawa|tr|Kakegawa|tt|Какегава|uk|Какеґава (Сідзуока)|ur|کاکیگاوا|vi|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|war|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|zh|掛川市|zh_classical|掛川市|zh_min_nan|Kakegawa-chhī|zh_yue|掛川|qid=Q823988}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takehinatori-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>, and its parishioners ({{ill|Ujiko|ja|氏子|qid=Q125562175}}) are the residents of Hinataga-tani, a {{ill|koaza|ja|小字|ko|고아자|zh|小字|qid=Q5327509}} of Kamitohata Ochiai<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>. Takehinatori-no-Mikoto is said to be a child deity of {{ill|Ame no Hohi|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/> and is traditionally believed to have played an active role, together with {{ill|Futsunushi|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1107286}}, in the {{ill|Kuni-yuzuri|br|Kuni-yuzuri|id|Kuni-yuzuri|it|Kuni-yuzuri|ja|国譲り|ko|위원중국 평정|zh|葦原中國平定|qid=Q11621119}}<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>. The shrine is identified with the shrine listed as “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="masamune1929_128">{{ill|Masamune Atsuo|fr|Atsuo Masamune|ja|正宗敦夫|qid=Q3297160}} (ed.), *Engishiki*, Vol. 2, Nihon Koten Zenshū Kankōkai, 1929, p. 128.</ref> in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} as a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|Q134917287|qid=Q134917287}}<ref name="mre1925_290">{{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|ja|教部省|ru|Министерство религий Японии|uk|Міністерство релігій Японії|qid=Q4294653}} (ed.), *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092|lt=Tokusen Jinmyōchō}}*, Isobe Kōyōdō, 1925, p. 290.</ref>.

=== History ===

Hinatano Shrine is located slightly north of the center of Kamitohata Ochiai, while Kegon-in, which formerly conducted the shrine’s rites, is located at the northern edge of Kamitohata Ochiai.]]
The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>. However, since two shrines—“Naranosha”<ref name="masamune1929_128"/> and “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="masamune1929_128"/>—are listed as {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|Q134917287|qid=Q134917287}} of {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikui District}} in Volume 9 of the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}*, compiled in 927 (the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}})<ref name="masamune1929_128"/><ref group="†">{{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikui District}} came to be written as {{ill|Kitō district|ja|城東郡|qid=Q11426221}} from the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} onward, and from the {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718}} onward was written exclusively as Jōtō District.</ref>, the founding of Hinatano Shrine is presumed to predate 927. The *Engishiki* is a legal code of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, compiled by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ca|Fujiwara no Tokihira|fa|فوجیوارا نو توکیهیرا|fr|Fujiwara no Tokihira|hr|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平|pl|Fujiwara no Tokihira|pt|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ru|Фудзивара-но Токихира|sh|Fujiwara no Tokihira|uk|Фудзівара но Токіхіра|zh|藤原時平|qid=Q2994735}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|Q1397601|qid=Q1397601}} under the order of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}. The lists of shrines recorded in Volumes 9 and 10 are known as the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, and shrines listed therein are called {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

Since its founding, the shrine has been located in Hinataga-tani of Ochiai Village, Kikui District, Tōtōmi Province<ref group="†">{{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikui District}} Ochiai Village later belonged to {{ill|Kitō district|ja|城東郡|qid=Q11426221}}.</ref>. During the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, it came to be known as “Tempaku Koma Shrine”<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>. With the advent of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}, it was positioned as the {{ill|Chinjusha|Q13479654|qid=Q13479654}} of the nearby {{ill|Buddhist temple|ar|معبد بوذي|bh|बौद्ध मंदिर|bn|বৌদ্ধ মন্দির|de|Buddhistischer Tempel|es|Templo budista|et|Budistlik tempel|fa|معبد بودایی|fi|Buddhalainen temppeli|fr|Temple bouddhiste|id|Tempat ibadah buddhis|it|Tempio buddista|ja|寺院|kn|ಬೌದ್ಧ ದೇವಾಲಯ|ko|사찰|mai|बौद्ध मन्दिर|mr|बौद्ध मंदिर|nl|Boeddhistische tempel|nn|Buddhisttempel|no|Buddhistisk tempel|pt|Templo budista|ro|Templu budist|si|බෞද්ධ පන්සල්|sl|Budistični tempelj|sv|Buddhistiska tempel|tr|Budist tapınağı|ur|بدھ مندر|vi|Chùa|wuu|佛寺|zh|佛寺|zh_min_nan|Hu̍t-sī|zh_yue|佛寺|qid=Q5393308}} Kegon-in<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/><ref name="mre1925_290"/>, and the shrine’s rites were thereafter conducted by Kegon-in<ref name="mre1925_290"/>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, the shrine’s name was restored to “Hinatano Shrine” in 1878 (the 11th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}})<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>. Having been ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>, its rites were administered by the government until 1945 (the 20th year of {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}})<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>.

=== Examination concerning the Shikinaisha ===
=== Engishiki ===
[[File:Engishiki cropped Engishiki Vol 2 Flame 69.jpg|thumb|200px|The section in Volume 9 of the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* included in the *Nihon Koten Zenshū* that records “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="masamune1929_128"/>.]]
The shrine’s origin record explicitly states that it is “one of the two shrines of Kikui District ({{ill|Kitō district|ja|城東郡|qid=Q11426221}}) listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō”<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>, and Hinatano Shrine is thus regarded as a Shikinaisha recorded in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō<ref name="mre1925_290"/>. However, because the Engishiki dates back to the Heian period, there are many Shikinaisha whose descendants became difficult to identify over time. As a result, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kokugaku scholars}} have long pursued research to identify the descendants of Shikinaisha, and the successor of the “Hinatano-no-sha” listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō has been discussed repeatedly.

=== Jinmyōchō kōshō ===
[[File:Ban Nobutomo Zenshu cropped Ban Nobutomo Zenshu Vol 1 Frame 121.jpg|thumb|200px|The section in *Jinmyōchō Kōshō Doyo* included in *Ban Nobutomo Zenshū* that discusses “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="ichishima1907_226">{{ill|Kenkichi Ichishima|Q11480125|qid=Q11480125}} (ed.), *Ban Nobutomo Zenshū*, Vol. 1, {{ill|Kokusho Kankōkai (1905–1922)|Q28686029|qid=Q28686029}}, 1907, p. 226.</ref>.]]
The Edo-period kokugaku scholar {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} studied ancient shrines and authored *{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō Dodai|Q11588823|qid=Q11588823|lt=Jinmyōchō Kōshō}}*. In it, he discusses the “Hinatano-no-sha” of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō<ref name="masamune1929_128"/>, stating that its enshrined deity was “the child of {{ill|Ame no Hohi|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohihi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takehi-Nateru|Q11065428|qid=Q11065428}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tōtōmi Province no Miyatsuko}}”<ref name="ichishima1907_226"/>. He then introduces a theory identifying it with {{ill|Taka Tenjinja|Q11669115|qid=Q11669115}}, located on the summit of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mount Takatenjin}}, south of {{ill|Kakegawa-juku|Q3070229|qid=Q3070229|lt=Kakegawa Station}}<ref name="ichishima1907_226"/>, citing as evidence the presence of a mountain village called Hinataga-tani at the foot of Mount Takatenjin<ref name="ichishima1907_226"/>. At the same time, Ban also introduces the theory of the local kokugaku scholar {{ill|Kurita Hijimaro|Q6536151|qid=Q6536151}}<ref name="ichishima1907_226"/>, who proposed identifying the shrine with the small guardian shrine of Kegon-in located in Hinataga-tani of Hijikata District<ref name="ichishima1907_226"/>.

Notably, the enshrined deities of Takaten Shrine are {{ill|Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto}}, Ame-no-Hohihi-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sugawara no Michizane}}<ref name="takatenJinja">“Takaten Shrine.”</ref>, not Takehiratori-no-Mikoto<ref name="takatenJinja"/>. By contrast, Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai enshrines Takehinatori-no-Mikoto<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>, who is regarded as the same divine entity as Takehiratori-no-Mikoto.

Furthermore, Takaten Shrine is located in {{ill|Kamihijikataminemukai|Q131426754|qid=Q131426754}}, Kakegawa City, very close to Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai. Kamitohata Mineko and Kamitohata Ochiai are neighboring {{ill|ōaza|Q424857|qid=Q424857}} that both formerly belonged to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamitohata Village}} of {{ill|Kitō district|ja|城東郡|qid=Q11426221}}, {{ill|Hamamatsu Prefecture|Q11557878|qid=Q11557878}}<ref group="†">{{ill|Hamamatsu Prefecture|Q11557878|qid=Q11557878}}{{ill|Kitō district|ja|城東郡|qid=Q11426221}} Ochiai Village merged with Mineko Village and Dantsuke Shinden to form Kamitohata Village in 1875.</ref>. However, Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai is the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Hinataga-tani<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/> and is located within Hinataga-tani itself<ref name="hinatanoJinja201303"/>, whereas Takaten Shrine is not located in Hinataga-tani but merely in its vicinity.

=== Jinja Kakuroku ===
[[File:Jinja Kakuroku cropped Jinja Kakuroku Part Jo Frame 439.jpg|thumb|200px|The section in the upper volume of *{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}* that discusses “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="suzuka1902_857">{{ill|Suzuka Tsuratane|Q6536446|qid=Q6536446|lt=Nakatomi no Asomi Tomotane}} (comp.), “Tōtōmi Province,” in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Suzuka Yoshikujira}}’s works, ed. by {{ill|Inoue Yorikuni|Q6535302|qid=Q6535302}} and {{ill|Saeki Ariyoshi|Q11382847|qid=Q11382847}}, *Jinja Kakuroku*, Upper Volume, {{ill|Koten Kokyusho|Q11580997|qid=Q11580997}}, 1902, p. 857.</ref>.]]
Another Edo-period Shinto priest, {{ill|Suzuka Tsuratane|Q6536446|qid=Q6536446}}, also researched ancient shrines and authored *{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}*. In it, he states regarding the “Hinatano-no-sha” of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō<ref name="masamune1929_128"/> that “the enshrined deity and location are unclear”<ref name="suzuka1902_857"/>, suggesting that details of its successor shrine had already become unknown<ref name="suzuka1902_857"/>. He then introduces the theory identifying it with Takaten Shrine, citing the existence of Hinataga-tani at the foot of Mount Takatenjin as evidence<ref name="suzuka1902_857"/>. He also introduces Kurita Domaru’s theory identifying it with Hinatano Shrine, the guardian shrine of Kegon-in in Hinataga-tani<ref name="suzuka1902_857"/>.

=== Tokusen Jinmyōchō ===
[[File:Tokusen Jimmyocho cropped Tokusen Jimmyocho Frame 182.jpg|thumb|200px|The section in *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}* that discusses “Hinatano-no-sha”<ref name="mre1925_290"/>.]]
In the Meiji period, research into ancient shrines was also advanced by the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|ja|教部省|ru|Министерство религий Японии|uk|Міністерство релігій Японії|qid=Q4294653}}, one of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=central government ministries}}, and the results were published as the *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}*. Therein, the “Hinatano-no-sha” of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō<ref name="masamune1929_128"/> is recorded as “Hinatano-no-sha, also called Tempaku Koma Shrine”<ref name="mre1925_290"/>, and its location is clearly specified as Hinataga-tani, Ochiai Village ({{ill|Ogasa District, Shizuoka|Q7079825|qid=Q7079825}}{{ill|Hijikata|Q11423527|qid=Q11423527}} Ōaza {{ill|Kamihijikata|Q131527787|qid=Q131527787}}, {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} Hinatano-no-sha)<ref name="mre1925_290"/><ref group="†">{{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}{{ill|Ogasa District, Shizuoka|Q7079825|qid=Q7079825}}{{ill|Hijikata|Q11423527|qid=Q11423527}} later merged with {{ill|Sazuka|Q11383208|qid=Q11383208}} to form {{ill|Kitō|Q11426205|qid=Q11426205}} in 1955.</ref>, explicitly identifying it with Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai. As supporting evidence, it cites *Jinja Kakuroku*, as well as local traditions that Ochiai Village was the original site of the Shikinaisha<ref name="mre1925_290"/>, and records of Kegon-in indicating that Hinatano Shrine, also known as Tempaku Koma Shrine, was a Shikinaisha and the guardian shrine at the time of Kegon-in’s founding<ref name="mre1925_290"/>. Based on this evidence, the *Tokusen Jinmyōchō* identifies the “Hinatano-no-sha” of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō with Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai.

Thereafter, the successor of the “Hinatano-no-sha” of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō has generally been regarded as Hinatano Shrine in Kamitohata Ochiai. For example, the *History of Shizuoka Prefecture*, published in 1936 (Shōwa 11), states that the original location was Hinataga-tani, Hijikata Village, Ogasawara District, and that the present shrine is Hinatano Shrine at that site, making no mention of Takaten Shrine<ref name="shizuoka1936_698">*History of Shizuoka Prefecture*, Vol. 3, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}, 1936, p. 698.</ref>.

=== Precincts ===
The shrine buildings are constructed in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ichigensha nagare-zukuri}} style. The surrounding trees form a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine grove}}. Rice paddies and tea fields spread out around the precincts.
